## How to use the Roman Numerals Converter

Start by typing or pasting your number or Roman numeral. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Type or paste your number or roman numeral.
2. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
3. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Roman symbols are generally added; a smaller symbol before a larger one is subtracted, as in IV = 4 and IX = 9.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Roman Numerals Converter](/roman-numerals-converter) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.
